result.scope_note: The first interval spans 1787 to 1791 (Bill of Rights ratification). The second interval spans congressional proposal (September 25, 1789) to ratification completion (December 15, 1791). Both intervals concern the same Bill of Rights under the US Constitution.

explanation.text: The interval from Constitution signing (1787) to Bill of Rights ratification (1791) is 4 years, while the interval from congressional proposal (September 1789) to ratification (December 1791) is approximately 2 years and 3 months. The first interval exceeds the second.

Constitution signing occurred September 17, 1787 in Philadelphia (span 21). Congressional proposal of 12 amendments occurred September 25, 1789 (span 29 and 12). Bill of Rights ratified December 15, 1791 (span 33 and 14).
Madison proposed 19 amendments on June 8, 1789; 12 were approved September 25, 1789; 10 became the Bill of Rights upon ratification December 15, 1791 (spans 29, 31, 33).

excerpts.text: A bill of rights was overruled. -MORE- ADD ONE/BILL OF RIGHTS FAQS The Constitution was signed by 39 delegates on September 17, 1787, at the Pennsylvania State House, now known as Independence Hall, in Philadelphia.
Madison drafted 19 amendments, which he proposed to Congress on June 8, 1789.
These 12 were approved on September 25, 1789 and sent to the states for ratification.
The 10 amendments that are now known as the Bill of Rights were ratified on December 15, 1791, thus becoming a part of the Constitution.
